This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant is in appeal challenging the correctness of the judgment and order dated 31.12.2016 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and the Commissioner for Employee's Compensation,
Vijayapur (henceforth referred to as 'the Commissioner'), in ECA No.436/2014, by which the claim petition under Section 22 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (for short 'the EC Act, 1923'),
was rejected.
2. The claimant claimed that he was engaged as a driver in a Car bearing registration No.KA-28/N-0242.
He NC: 2023:KHC-K:1138 claimed that on 17.10.2012 when he was driving the car on Vijayapur-Solapur road, it met with an accident and he sustained injuries.
He was admitted at Dr. Shailesh Deshpande Hospital, Vijayapur.
He claimed that he was receiving Rs.6,000/- per month as wages and a sum of Rs.50/- per day as daily allowance.

He contended that due to the injuries, he was permanently disabled and therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 22 of the EC Act, 1923, claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the car.
3. The owner of the car denied the allegations made in the claim petition.
However, he admitted that the claimant was employed as a driver in the car and receiving wages at a sum of 6,000/- per month and daily allowance of Rs.50/-.
He also admitted that the accident happened in the course of employment, but denied the medical expenses incurred by the claimant.

4. The insurer of the car contested the claim petition and claimed that there was no relationship of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1138 employer and employee as the claimant was none other than the brother of the owner of the car.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.

sentences.text: The claimant was examined as P.W.1 and he marked Exs.P.1 to P.13.
He examined a doctor who did not treat the claimant, as P.W.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 15-20%.

The owner of the car was examined as R.W.1 and he marked Ex.R.1 while a representative of the insurer was examined as R.W.2 and Exs.R.2 to R.4 were marked.
6.
Based on oral and documentary evidence, the Commissioner held that the claimant was not a workman and there was no employer and employee relationship between the claimant and owner of the Car.
It held that the claimant had suffered fracture of left scapula and other injuries.
It assessed the compensation at a sum of Rs.60,885/- by treating the disability suffered by the claimant at 6%.

However, since the claimant did not establish the relationship of employer and employee, it NC:
2023:KHC-K:1138 dismissed the claim petition.
Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed.

7. Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the owner of the car did admit that the claimant was employed in the car and therefore, the insurer cannot dispute it only on the ground that the claimant and the owner of the car are related to each other by blood.

He contended that there is an implied contract between the claimant and respondent No.1 and therefore, the Commissioner could not have brushed aside the claim of the claimant that he was employed in the car.

He relied upon the judmgnet of the Apex Court in the case of T.S. Shylaja vs. Oriental Insurance Company and Another1 and contended that even if the parties are related by blood, that is not a ground to reject the claim of the claimant, who was employed under the owner.

entities.text: T.S. Shylaja vs. Oriental Insurance Company and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that the claimant was a brother of the owner of (2014) 2 SCC 587 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1138 the car and there was no express or implied contract of employment between them and therefore, a claim petition under the provisions of the EC Act, 1923, was not maintainable.

He further claimed that the claim petition is filed under the provisions of the EC Act, 1923, since no other vehicle was involved in the accident, the claimant must have been advised that a claim petition under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is not maintainable.

He therefore, contended that the claimant was unable to make out the relationship of employer and employee and hence, claim petition was not maintainable and the Commissioner rightly dismissed the claim petition and in this regard, the learned counsel for the insurer relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Gottumukkala Appala Narasimha Raju and Ors.
Vs. National Insurance Co.Ltd. and Ors.2 (2007) 13 SCC 446 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1138 9.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. and Ors.2 (2007) 13 SCC 446 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1138
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
10. The insurer did not dispute the fact that it was bound to indemnify the owner for the damages caused to the Car.
The fact that the claimant and the owner of the car are related to each other is not in much dispute.
The fact that the claimant rode the Car which belonged to his brother did imply the engagement of the claimant under an implied contract.
The relationship of the parties cannot deprive the beneficial object of the legislation.
The owner of the Car who contested the claim petition had admitted that he was paying a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month as salary to the claimant along with a sum of Rs.50/- per day as daily allowance.

The insurer could not establish that this Praveen S/O Kallappa Baratagi vs Sri.Harish And Anr on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129122252/
3 contention of the owner was false.

entities.text: Praveen S/O Kallappa Baratagi vs Sri.Harish And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, it is appropriate that the claimant is suitably compensated.

Consequently, the compensation to which the claimant is entitled to is assessed as follows:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1138 i).

Compensation for the injuries: Rs.3,600 x 60% x 216.9 x 10% = Rs.46,850/-
ii).

Medical expenses : Rs.2,229/-
Total compensation payable Rs.49,079/-.
In view of the above, the claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.49,079/-.

Consequently,
the appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and order passed by the Commissioner is set aside.

The insurer of the Car is directed to pay the compensation of Rs.49,079/- along with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. with effect from the date of accident till its realization.
The insurer of the car is directed to deposit the compensation and interest within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
